sources.entry: django-cacheops - A slick ORM cache with automatic granular event-driven invalidation.

summary.one_liner: django-cacheops is a Django app that adds automatic, event-driven invalidated ORM queryset caching backed by Redis, plus time-based function, view and template-fragment caching.
summary.what_it_does: Caches Django ORM query results (get, fetch, count, aggregate, exists) in Redis and invalidates them automatically when relevant model rows change, with per-model rules set in a CACHEOPS settings dict. It supports manual per-queryset caching via .cache() and opting out via .nocache(). Decorators @cached and @cached_as cache arbitrary functions or views by time or by queryset dependency, and template fragment caching is available for Django templates and a Jinja2 extension. Redis can be configured by dict, URL, or Sentinel, and the README describes transaction handling, dog-pile lock prevention, and a reapconjs command for cleaning up leftover invalidation sets. Simple time-invalidated caching can use redis or the filesystem.
use_cases: speed up slow Django ORM queries
automatically invalidate cached querysets on model changes
cache expensive Django view or function results
share a Redis instance across multiple Django sites
how_to_run: Set CACHEOPS_REDIS to a Redis host dict or URL such as redis://localhost:6379/1
Configure the CACHEOPS dict to choose models and ops to cache, e.g. 'auth.*': {'ops': {'fetch', 'get'}, 'timeout': 3600}
Use Model.objects.filter(...).cache() for manual caching or @cached_as(Model) for functions
notable: Automatic granular invalidation driven by model signals, keyed on simple field conditions such as exact match, __in and __isnull=True
Transaction-aware: caching turns off while a transaction is dirty and invalidation runs on outer commit
Dog-pile prevention via lock=True on cached_as and querysets
Supports Redis Sentinel, Unix sockets, and a custom Redis client class
Cache read and invalidation signals for collecting hit/miss stats
caveats: Several query conditions do not invalidate granularly (non-exact lookups, text/file/binary fields, select_related updates), and mass updates do not invalidate by default
Does not work with raw SQL or .raw(), and does not work correctly with multi-table inheritance
Requires a running Redis 4.0+ server; needs Python 3.8+ and Django 3.2+
